Everyone moves down to the x3 row, and consumption doubles with it. No disasters this year. New land is open at twenty a square. Silke, the crown is allowed to pay part of it, so I suggest you think about who's going to pay your tax next year.

Storyteller's tip: the crown may pay any part of a province's square, up to all of it, and every square it helps buy raises that province's income, and so the tax it can pay. Your own board card shows how many squares Province 1 needs to break even.

Nobody owes a grain this year, so I won't pretend to collect one. Ten percent on nothing is nothing. Reina, here's the coast canal I said was coming, the first section of it, paid for by the crown. And every one of you who breaks new ground this year gets half of each square from me. Buy land. A hungry province is no use to me or to you.

Nobody's income is positive, so the 10% tax raises nothing. Silke digs the first section of the Grand Canal in Province 5 for 40 (+10 to Reina's harvest from next year; 280 still owed), and buys two sea squares for Province 1, F23 and F24, for 40. The crown offers 10 of every square another province buys this year. The crown's reserve is now 40, and Graham's 5 is still to be paid at the end of the year.

Storyteller's tip: a square bought this year starts yielding with next year's harvest and pays for itself in a year. Your board card shows how many you need to break even, now and after the next card. A player in debt can't buy any.

Silke, that's a promise kept in front of everyone and I'll say so: the coast canal is dug. I'll take you up on the half, two squares on the coast, ten from me and ten from the crown on each. A fed Province 5 pays you tax next year instead of a revolt.
Reina buys two sea squares for Province 5, O27 and P27, paying 10 of each and the crown 10. Reina has 5 left; the crown's reserve is 20, with Graham's 5 still to be paid.

Storyteller's tip: a square bought this year starts yielding with next year's harvest and pays for itself in a year. Your board card shows how many you need to break even, now and after the next card. A player in debt can't buy any.

Thank you, Silke, I'll take you at your word, same as Reina did: two squares of paddy on the coast, R25 and R26, ten from me and ten from the crown on each. Rice doesn't grow on promises, but it grows on new mud right enough.

Paddy buys two sea squares for Province 6, R25 and R26, paying 10 of each and the crown 10. Paddy has 29.5 left. The crown's reserve is now 0: the Emperor must pay part of every other province's square (Section 13), so the crown can't share in another square this year unless it gets grain from somewhere.

Storyteller's tip: a square bought this year starts yielding with next year's harvest and pays for itself in a year. Your board card shows how many you need to break even, now and after the next card. A player in debt can't buy any.

Silke, your purse is empty, but you owe me five for the reading, and the rules say the crown pays some part of every square. So pay one grain a square out of what you owe me and I'll pay the other nineteen. Three squares of wheat in Province 7, and you don't have to find a grain you haven't got.

Graham, that's the most gracious way anyone has ever asked me for money I don't have. Done. One grain a square from your salary, three squares of wheat for Province 7, and I still owe you two at year's end. Write it down so nobody says the crown forgot.

Silke accepts Graham's terms. The crown has no grain, so Graham hands it 3 against this year's I Ching salary and the crown pays that back as its 1 a square. Graham buys T15, T16 and T17 for Province 7, 60 in all (57 from him, 3 from the crown), and has 43.5 left. By their deal the crown still owes Graham 2 for the year. Silke buys no more squares.
